deed: לודוויג גוטמן, רופא יהודי שנמלט מגרמניה, ארגן ב-1948 את משחקי סטוק מנדוויל ופתח את דרכה של הפראלימפיאדה
title: Ludwig Guttmann, a Jewish doctor who fled the Nazis, organised games in 1948 that gave rise to the Paralympics

trailer.text: Ludwig Guttmann was a Jewish neurosurgeon who left Nazi Germany with his family in 1939, according to the Science Museum, and Google Arts & Culture calls him the father of the Paralympic Movement.

According to the Royal College of Physicians, the British government asked him to set up a centre for spinal injuries at Stoke Mandeville Hospital, and according to the UK National Archives he encouraged his patients there to take up sport.
According to the International Paralympic Committee, the first games were held at Stoke Mandeville on 29 July 1948, and 16 injured servicemen and women competed in them in archery.
According to the Wellcome Collection, by 1956, 18 nations took part in the games, including Israel.
According to Google Arts & Culture, the games held immediately after the Rome Olympics are recognised as the first Paralympic Games.

stations.title: A boy from Tost, a doctor in Breslau

paragraphs.text: According to the Royal Society, Ludwig Guttmann was born on 3 July 1899 to a German Jewish family in Tost.
The town was then in the German Empire, and today it is Toszek in southern Poland.
According to the UK National Archives, he grew up in the city of Königshütte, today Chorzów, Poland.
By 1937 he had become medical director of the Jewish Hospital in Breslau, and was responsible for medical and nursing education.
He was also chairman of the Jewish Medical Association.

stations.title: Kristallnacht, and the road to England

paragraphs.text: According to History Hit, after Kristallnacht, on 9 November 1938, Guttmann ordered the hospital staff to admit all patients without asking questions.
According to his daughter Eva Loeffler, he insisted to the Gestapo that all the men were sick, and that many of them were suffering from stress.
According to History Hit, out of 64 admissions, 60 were saved from arrest and deportation to concentration camps.
According to the Royal College of Physicians, the Nazis ordered Guttmann not to leave Breslau.
According to the Royal Society, in 1939 Guttmann was ordered to Portugal to treat a friend of the dictator Salazar, and this was the opportunity to escape.
According to the Royal Society, in London the SPSL arranged for Guttmann and his family to remain in Britain.
According to his daughter, he had to begin living and working in England at the age of 40, with a poor grasp of the language, and unable to continue his career as a neurologist and neurosurgeon.
According to a card in the Aliens Department records at the UK National Archives, he was given full exemption from internment as an enemy alien.
According to the Royal Society, he continued his spinal injury research at the Nuffield Department of Neurosurgery at the Radcliffe Infirmary in Oxford.

stations.title: "Hopeless cases": the centre at Stoke Mandeville

paragraphs.text: According to Historic England, before Guttmann, people with spinal paralysis were seen as "hopeless cases".
According to the Royal College of Physicians, before the Second World War an injury of the spinal cord was virtually a death sentence.
According to the British National Archives, in the forties many cases ended in death because of pressure sores.
According to History Hit, the life expectancy of paraplegics at the time was around two years from the time of injury.
According to the Royal College of Physicians, in 1944 the Government asked him to set up the first special centre for spinal injuries, at Stoke Mandeville Hospital.
According to the Royal Society, the centre was intended to help Royal Air Force pilots injured in crash landings, and according to Google Arts & Culture it was intended for war veterans.
According to History Hit, Guttmann accepted the directorship on the condition that he could treat his patients however he chose.
According to the UK National Archives, the centre opened in 1944, and Guttmann, two nurses and eight orderlies worked there.
According to History Hit, within six months of the opening Guttmann had nearly 50 patients.
According to the Royal College of Physicians, the unit expanded over some fifteen years to 192 beds.
According to the Wellcome Collection, it was the first specialist unit of its kind, and as of 2021 it is one of the largest in the world.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, Guttmann reduced the death rate of paraplegics from over 80% to under 10% within three years of injury.
According to the same encyclopaedia, the British minister of pensions said in 1945: "Thank you, Hitler, for sending us men like these."
According to Historic England, it all began in 1944 with a competitive "dressing exercise" on Ward X.
In it, young paralysed men competed to be the first to get out of bed, get dressed and move into a wheelchair.
According to the UK National Archives, Guttmann believed that physical movement was essential to rehabilitation, and encouraged his patients to take up sport.
According to the Science Museum, the exercise was intended to develop strong upper bodies, as the patients could not walk.
According to the Wellcome Collection, Guttmann and a colleague introduced darts, snooker, table tennis, skittles and archery into rehabilitation.
According to the Science Museum, Guttmann also invented wheelchair polo, but the players suffered severe injuries in most games, so they did not play it for long.
According to History Hit, archery was popular because it relied on upper body strength, so paraplegics could compete against non-disabled people.
According to his daughter, Guttmann himself was not a sportsman.
But he realised how important sport was, in giving his patients an interest in life and in having society accept them.
According to the International Paralympic Committee, the first Stoke Mandeville Games were held on 29 July 1948, and 16 injured servicemen and women competed in them in archery.
According to Google Arts & Culture, they were 14 men and two women.
According to Historic England, they competed against a team from the Star and Garter home for war-disabled people in Richmond.
According to the UK National Archives, the competition coincided with the opening of the London Olympics, on the same day.
According to his daughter Eva Loeffler, in his opening speech Guttmann said that he dreamed of a day when there would be Olympic Games for people with disabilities.
According to the Royal Society, he aimed to create an elite sports competition for people with disabilities that would be the equivalent of the Olympic Games.
According to Historic England, he predicted that one day these games would be the disabled person's equivalent of the Olympics.

stations.title: From an annual event to the Paralympics

paragraphs.text: According to the Wellcome Collection, from 1948 the "paraplegic games" became an annual event at Stoke Mandeville.
According to Historic England, in 1950 the games were named the Stoke Mandeville Festival of Sport.
According to the same source, in 1950, 10,000 people watched a wheelchair netball match at the Empress Hall in west London.

The National Paralympic Heritage Trust page on Google Arts & Culture shows a photograph captioned "Israeli team at the Stoke Mandeville Games (1950)", but the same page states that the first international Stoke Mandeville Games took place only in 1952, so the date in the caption does not agree with the text.
Google Arts & Culture and Historic England give 1952 as the year the games became international.
According to Google Arts & Culture, that year a small team of veterans from the Netherlands came to Stoke Mandeville.
According to the Wellcome Collection, by 1956, 18 nations took part in the games, including the USA, Australia, Israel, South Africa, Malaya and Pakistan.
According to the Royal College of Physicians, at the 1956 Melbourne Olympic Games the Olympic Committee awarded the Fearnley Cup to the organization of the Stoke Mandeville Games.
According to Google Arts & Culture, the International Stoke Mandeville Games were held immediately after the Rome Olympics, and they are recognised as the first Paralympic Games.
According to the Wellcome Collection, the 1960 Rome games were not an official Olympic event, but most consider them the first Paralympic Games.
According to the Wellcome Collection, the 1964 Tokyo games were the first to use the name "Paralympics", but the International Olympic Committee officially approved it only in 1984.
According to the same source, in 1989 the International Paralympic Committee was founded as the governing body, and in this way the link between the Olympic and Paralympic Games was established.
According to the International Paralympic Committee, the Rome games took place from 18 to 25 September 1960.
According to Historic England, 4,200 disabled athletes took part in 20 sports at the London 2012 games, in accessible venues.
According to the UK National Archives, the mascot of those Paralympics was named Mandeville, in recognition of the movement's origins at Stoke Mandeville.
Sources disagree on whether the Paralympics are the second or the third biggest sporting event.
According to the UK National Archives, Guttmann's work was recognised with an OBE in 1950, a knighthood in 1966 and election as a Fellow of the Royal Society in 1976.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, in 1953 he received the Rehabilitation Prize of the World Veterans' Association, and was its first recipient.
According to the Wellcome Collection, he was President of the International Stoke Mandeville Games, and founded the British Sports Association for the Disabled.
According to the International Paralympic Committee, in 1972 he flew to his native Germany to celebrate the fourth Paralympic Games in Heidelberg.

According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, in 1972, at the 21st International Stoke Mandeville Games in Heidelberg, German President Heinemann bestowed upon him the Star of the Grand Cross of the Order of Merit of the Federal Republic, West Germany's highest award.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, as a result of his visit to Israel in 1949, a paraplegic centre was opened at Tel Ha-Shomer in 1953.
According to the same source, Sir Ludwig Guttmann and Lady Guttmann were active in the local Jewish community and supported Israel in many ways.
According to the Royal College of Physicians, he lectured and advised on the treatment and rehabilitation of paraplegia in over thirty countries.

According to the Royal Society, at a conference in 1956 Guttmann said that it was necessary not only to save lives, but also to give paraplegics back their dignity and make them happy and respected citizens.
According to the Royal College of Physicians, he saved and made worthwhile the lives of many thousands of severely disabled people all over the world.
According to Google Arts & Culture, Guttmann died on 18 March 1980, aged 80.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, Guttmann's ideas on rehabilitating people with spinal injuries were highly original, and at the time controversial.
In a government visit report dated 25 October 1948, the official wrote that he was disappointed in the industrial resettlement side at the hospital, and criticised a lack of planning.
The same report described Guttmann as a skilled specialist with a broad outlook, doing magnificent work and determined to get his patients back to a self-supporting life.
According to his daughter Eva Loeffler, he retained a "Germanic" authoritarian strain, and it was difficult to argue with him.

claims.text: לפי בתו, גוטמן עצמו לא היה ספורטאי, אך הבין עד כמה הספורט חשוב למתן עניין בחיים למטופליו ולקבלתם בחברה.
claims.quote: Although not a sportsman himself, he realised how important sport was in giving his patients an interest in life and accepting them in society.

claims.text: לפי Google Arts & Culture, במשחקים הראשונים התחרו 16 מטופלים, 14 גברים ושתי נשים, בחץ וקשת.
claims.quote: 16 patients (14 men and 2 women) competed in archery. These Games were the birth of the Paralympic Movement.

claims.text: לפי Historic England, ב-29 ביולי 1948 נערכה בסטוק מנדוויל תחרות קשתות מול קבוצה מבית הלוחמים הנכים סטאר אנד גרטר בריצ'מונד.
claims.quote: an archery competition took place on the lawns of Stoke Mandeville against a team from the Star and Garter residential home for war-disabled people in Richmond, Surrey

claims.text: לפי בתו אווה לפלר, גוטמן אמר בנאום הפתיחה ב-1948 שהוא חולם על יום שבו יתקיימו משחקים אולימפיים לאנשים עם מוגבלויות.
claims.quote: In his welcoming speech in 1948 he said: ‘I dream of the day when there will be Olympic Games for people with disabilities.’

claims.text: לפי החברה המלכותית, גוטמן שאף ליצור תחרות ספורט עילית לאנשים עם מוגבלות שתהיה המקבילה למשחקים האולימפיים.
claims.quote: He aimed to create an elite sports competition for people with disabilities that would be the equivalent of the Olympic Games.

claims.text: לפי Historic England, גוטמן ניבא שיום אחד המשחקים יהיו המקבילה של האולימפיאדה לאנשים עם מוגבלות.
claims.quote: Guttman predicted that one day it would become the disabled person's equivalent of the Olympics.

claims.text: לפי Wellcome Collection, מ-1948 "משחקי המשותקים" הפכו לאירוע שנתי בסטוק מנדוויל.
claims.quote: From 1948, the “paraplegic games” became an annual event at Stoke Mandeville.

claims.text: לפי Historic England, ב-1950 נקראו המשחקים פסטיבל הספורט של סטוק מנדוויל, ו-10,000 איש צפו במשחק כדורסל כיסאות גלגלים באולם אמפרס בלונדון.
claims.quote: In 1950 the games were named the Stoke Mandeville Festival of Sport, and 10,000 people watched a wheelchair netball match at the Empress Hall in west London.

claims.text: לפי כיתוב תמונה ב-Google Arts & Culture, נבחרת ישראלית השתתפה במשחקי סטוק מנדוויל ב-1950.
claims.quote: Israeli team at the Stoke Mandeville Games (1950)National Paralympic Heritage Trust

claims.text: לפי Google Arts & Culture, ב-1952 הגיעה קבוצה קטנה של ותיקי צבא מהולנד לסטוק מנדוויל, וזה היה המשחקים הבינלאומיים הראשונים.
claims.quote: In 1952, a small team of veterans from the Military Rehabilitation Centre at Aardenburg in the Netherlands travelled to Stoke Mandeville to compete against a number of British Teams.

claims.text: לפי Historic England, ב-1952 המשחקים הפכו לבינלאומיים, ועד 1966 ברומא השתתפו 400 ספורטאים עם מוגבלות מ-22 מדינות.
claims.quote: In 1952 the games became international and by 1966, in Rome, 400 disabled athletes from 22 countries were participating.

claims.text: לפי הקולג' המלכותי לרופאים, באולימפיאדת מלבורן ב-1956 העניקה הוועדה האולימפית את גביע פרנלי לארגון משחקי סטוק מנדוויל, לראשונה לארגון ספורט לנכים קשים.
claims.quote: During the Olympic Games in Melbourne in 1956, the Olympic Committee awarded the Fearnley Cup to the organization of the Stoke Mandeville Games.

claims.text: לפי Google Arts & Culture, ב-1956 הוענק לגוטמן עצמו גביע סר תומאס פרנלי מהוועד האולימפי הבינלאומי על שירותו לתנועה האולימפית.
claims.quote: At the 1956 Stoke Mandeville Games, Guttmann was awarded the Sir Thomas Fearnley Cup by the International Olympic Committee for his service to the Olympic movement.

claims.text: לפי Wellcome Collection, משחקי רומא 1960 לא היו אירוע אולימפי רשמי, אך רובם רואים בהם את הפראלימפיאדה הראשונה.
claims.quote: Although not an official Olympic event, they are considered by most to be the first Paralympic Games.

claims.text: לפי Wellcome Collection, משחקי טוקיו 1964 היו הראשונים שהשתמשו בשם "פראלימפיאדה", אך הוועד האולימפי הבינלאומי אישר אותו רשמית רק ב-1984.
claims.quote: They were the first to use the name ‘Paralympics’ too, although the term was not officially approved by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) until 1984.

claims.text: לפי Wellcome Collection, הקשר בין המשחקים האולימפיים לפראלימפיים נקבע ב-1989 עם הקמת הוועד הפראלימפי הבינלאומי כגוף המנהל.
claims.quote: The link between the Olympic Games and the Paralympic Games was firmly established in 1989 by the foundation of the International Paralympic Committee (IPC) as the governing body of the Games.

claims.text: לפי הארכיון הלאומי הבריטי, הקמע של פראלימפיאדת לונדון 2012 נקרא מנדוויל כהוקרה למקורות התנועה בסטוק מנדוויל.
claims.quote: In recognition of the origins of the Paralympics at Stoke Mandeville Hospital, the Paralympic mascot at the London 2012 Paralympics was named Mandeville.

claims.text: לפי בתו של גוטמן (2018), הפראלימפיאדה היא האירוע הספורטיבי השלישי בגודלו אחרי האולימפיאדה וגביע העולם בכדורגל.
claims.quote: his legacy is the modern Paralympic Games, now the third biggest sporting event after the Olympic Games and the Football World Cup.

claims.text: לפי Historic England, הפראלימפיאדה היא האירוע הספורטיבי השני בגודלו בעולם.
claims.quote: Today the Paralympics are the second biggest sporting event in the world.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, ב-1953 קיבל גוטמן את פרס השיקום של ארגון הוותיקים העולמי, והיה הזוכה הראשון בו.
claims.quote: The many honors bestowed upon him include the Rehabilitation Prize of the World Veterans' Association in 1953 (he was the first recipient).

claims.text: לפי Wellcome Collection, גוטמן היה נשיא משחקי סטוק מנדוויל הבינלאומיים והקים את האגודה הבריטית לספורט לנכים.
claims.quote: As well as being President of the International Stoke Mandeville Games, he founded the British Sports Association for the Disabled.

claims.text: לפי הוועד הפראלימפי הבינלאומי, גוטמן טס לגרמניה מולדתו לחגוג את המשחקים הפראלימפיים הרביעיים בהיידלברג ב-1972.
claims.quote: Guttmann would fly back to his home country to celebrate the fourth Paralympic Games in Heidelberg, in 1972.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, ב-1972 העניק לו נשיא גרמניה היינמן את עיטור הכוכב של צלב הכבוד הגדול, ההוקרה הגבוהה ביותר של מערב גרמניה, במשחקים בהיידלברג.
claims.quote: In 1972 President Heinemann bestowed upon him the Star of the Grand Cross of the Order of Merit of the Federal Republic, West Germany's highest award

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, בעקבות ביקורו בישראל ב-1949 נפתח ב-1953 מרכז לשיתוק בתל השומר.
claims.quote: as a result of his visit to Israel in 1949 the paraplegic center at Tel Ha-Shomer was opened in 1953

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, סר לודוויג ולייפי גוטמן פעלו בקהילה היהודית המקומית ותמכו בישראל בדרכים רבות.
claims.quote: Both Sir Ludwig and Lady Guttmann were active in the local Jewish community and supported Israel's cause in many ways.

claims.text: לפי הקולג' המלכותי לרופאים, גוטמן הרצה וייעץ על טיפול ושיקום בשיתוק ביותר משלושים מדינות.
claims.quote: his hard work and dedication to Stoke Mandeville did not prevent him from finding time to lecture and advise on the treatment and rehabilitation of paraplegia in over thirty countries

claims.text: לפי החברה המלכותית, גוטמן אמר בכנס ב-1956 שהיה צריך לא רק להציל חיים אלא גם להחזיר למשותקים את כבודם ולהפוך אותם לאזרחים מאושרים ומכובדים.
claims.quote: we had not only to save the life of these paraplegic or quadriplegic men, women and children but also give them back their dignity and make them happy and respected citizens.

claims.text: לפי הקולג' המלכותי לרופאים, גוטמן הציל והעניק משמעות לחייהם של אלפים רבים של אנשים עם מוגבלות קשה ברחבי העולם.
claims.quote: Guttmann saved and made worthwhile the lives of many thousands of severely disabled people all over the world

claims.text: לפי Google Arts & Culture, גוטמן מת ב-18 במרץ 1980 בגיל 80.
claims.quote: On the 18th March 1980, Guttmann died aged 80 years of age.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, רעיונותיו של גוטמן לשיקום פגועי עמוד שדרה היו מקוריים מאוד ובזמנו שנויים במחלוקת.
claims.quote: highly original – and at the time controversial – ideas on rehabilitating persons suffering from irreversible spinal injuries that resulted in paraplegia

claims.text: בדוח ביקור ממשלתי מ-25 באוקטובר 1948 כתב הפקיד שהוא מאוכזב מצד ההשמה התעסוקתית בבית החולים, וביקר חוסר תכנון.
claims.quote: I wish I could say the same about the industrial resettlement side. From the brief impressions I gained through our afternoon's visit I felt very disappointed in our side of the work

claims.text: בדוח הביקור הממשלתי מ-25 באוקטובר 1948 תואר גוטמן כמומחה מיומן, בעל השקפה רחבה, שעושה עבודה מופלאה ונחוש להחזיר את מטופליו לחיים עצמאיים.
claims.quote: He is obviously a skilled specialist, with a broad outlook, doing magnificent work, determined to get his patients back to a self-supporting life.

claims.text: לפי בתו אווה לפלר, גוטמן שמר על קו סמכותני "גרמני" והיה קשה להתווכח איתו.
claims.quote: He retained that very Germanic strain of authoritarianism. It was difficult to disagree or argue with him.

claims.text: לפי הוועד הפראלימפי הבינלאומי, משחקי רומא נערכו בין 18 ל-25 בספטמבר 1960.
claims.quote: They took place from 18 to 25 September 1960.

claims.text: עד 1937 הוא כבר הפך למנהל הרפואי של בית החולים היהודי בברסלאו, והיה אחראי על הכשרה רפואית וסיעודית.
claims.quote: by 1937 had become medical director and was responsible for medical and nursing education

Life-size bronze statue of Sir Ludwig Guttmann, leaning against a stone wall engraved with his name, at Stoke Mandeville Hospital.
